title: R8, Resource Shrinking, Rules, Mapping, and Symbols Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies r8, resource shrinking, rules, mapping, and symbols?
options: Test optimised release behaviour and retain exact versioned mapping and native symbols for diagnosis.
Use consumer rules to hide all library internals
questions.answer: Test optimised release behaviour and retain exact versioned mapping and native symbols for diagnosis.
questions.explanation: This answer preserves the underlying platform or delivery contract while requiring representative evidence, explicit failure behaviour, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: An R8 mapping file from the same source revision is sufficient even if the final build differs.
questions.explanation: Keeping every class in a package to fix one reflection failure disables useful shrinking and can conceal an undocumented runtime contract.

questions.prompt: Why are mapping and native symbols release-specific?
questions.answer: Optimisation and linking assign names and addresses for exact binary bytes; another build can map stacks incorrectly.
questions.explanation: The response identifies the mechanism that makes the decision reliable instead of relying on a convenient proxy.
